title: The Savoy as a safe place for Harlem's youth
summary: For about a dollar young people spent hours at the Savoy, and Holmes laments that nothing like it exists now.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, what was the mood of Harlem in those days? Everybody pulling together? Everybody having a good time? Everybody trying to...?

Well, people were having a good time, because... First thing, it's composed of a lot of poor people -- poor young people. But you see, they had some place to go. I'm not speaking of the (?). You'd hear the talking.. The young people had some place to go for entertainment.

They had the Savoy Ballroom to go to. And I think at that time the admission was around a dollar, maybe a little bit under that. Now, they could go to the Savoy Ballroom, which could hold six thousand people, and it was a beautiful ballroom, and they always had two bands playing, continuous music, a beautiful place, you could and meet people or you could just go there and sit and enjoy the music, or you could go and sit over there in a booth and you could get food served to you -- anything. I mean, the atmosphere was so conducive to keep you on a down(?) (?). You know what I mean? I mean, you were so contented. So you could sit up there and imagine you were this-that-or-the-other, because the place was a beautiful place.

And these people would spend a dollar or less to come in there, and they could come in there and sometimes stay in there five and six hours at a time. Well, that will take you off the street a whole lot of hours. And that's where all the youngsters would go. They'd go up there and learn how to dance, and they'd have different games and things for them. It was beautiful. It was really beautiful.

Now they don't have any place like that, the youngsters who come along. And I'm glad they don't have a place like that now, with all this corruption and one thing and another that they have, because...

Oh, conditions are terrible now. I mean, life doesn't mean anything no more. Not only wreck the place, they'd kill off a whole lot of people. The Savoy, nothing ever happened there. You never had no big... I don't remember any altercations happening there that even made the newspapers. I never heard of anybody getting killed there or beat up so bad that it even made the newspapers. Very little things happened there. Everybody went there to have a good time. They enjoyed themselves. Just like people going to the Roseland. You've heard of the Roseland.

Well, the Savoy looked better than most of the Roseland did. I think it was a little larger than the Roseland. I'm not sure of the capacity of the Roseland, but they were built on the same order. And the Roseland went for years and years and years. You'd never read nothin' in the newspaper about the Roseland unless it was some affair or something that was coming off. You'd never hear nothin' detrimental against it. You'd never hear of nobody gettin' killed in the Roseland or gettin' beat up or this-that-and-the-other. Same thing with the Savoy.
Well, people seemed to want to dance to the music.
That's right. Well, that's what they were doing at the Savoy. They was dancin'. They was up there dancin'. Yeah, they was dancin'.
